install.title: Install
install.description: Install Tuix with Bun and add the packages for a terminal app.

sections.heading: Requirements
sections.body: Use Bun 1.1 or newer. Run Tuix on macOS, Linux, or Windows. Use Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) for Pseudo-Terminal (PTY) work.

sections.heading: Install from the monorepo
sections.body: Clone the repository. Install the dependencies. Run the tests and the type checks.
sections.code:
git clone https://github.com/vibesdotdev/tuix.git
cd tuix
bun install
bun test
bun run typecheck
bun run lint

sections.heading: Add packages to an app
sections.body: Workspace packages publish under the @tuix scope. Add the foundation packages for a new app. You can also link packages with Bun workspaces from a local checkout.

sections.heading: Run the CLI
sections.body: Run the tuix command from the monorepo. Use --help to list commands. Use version to print the version string.
sections.code:
bun run tuix --help
bun packages/bin/src/bin/tuix.ts version

sections.heading: What to do next
sections.body: Open the Quickstart guide. Build a first JSX app. Then read the Architecture guide for layers and Model-View-Update (MVU).

quickstart.title: Quickstart
quickstart.description: Build a terminal app with JSX, named state, and Model-View-Update (MVU).

sections.heading: What you build
sections.body: Tuix is a terminal UI framework for Bun. You write JSX components. The runtime compiles each component into Model-View-Update (MVU). Side effects run through Effect.

sections.heading: Counter with named state
sections.body: Create state with $state and a name. The name keeps the model field after compile under Bun. Call runApp with extractState set to true. The runtime hydrates named state from the model on each paint.

sections.heading: Update state
sections.body: Use $set to change a named field. $set sends a set message into MVU through bindMvuPush. The next paint reads the new value from the model. You can also create many fields with $states.

sections.heading: Register CLI commands
sections.body: Use the Command component for each subcommand. Use Fallback for a bare invocation with no subcommand. Call runApp on the root app component.

sections.heading: Provide live terminal services
sections.body: Import LiveServices from @tuix/platform. Provide the layer to Effect programs that need terminal input and output. Live implementations live under @tuix/core. The platform package re-exports them for apps.

sections.heading: Run the tests
sections.body: Run the monorepo suite with bun test. Run architecture tests to check package import direction.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.description: Describe Tuix layers, Model-View-Update (MVU) data flow, and I/O ownership.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Tuix is a Bun-native terminal UI framework. Apps use JSX as the primary authoring form. State and side effects run through an Effect-powered Model-View-Update (MVU) loop.

sections.heading: Layers
sections.body: Packages sit in four layers. Foundation holds core, ansi, input, platform, and storage. Runtime holds view, runtime, and reactive. Authoring holds jsx, ui, and themes. Ecosystem holds process-manager, config, testing, bin, and related packages. Lower layers never import higher layers. Architecture tests enforce this rule.

sections.heading: Data flow
sections.body: JSX compiles to a component with init, update, and view. The MVU loop owns the model. RuntimeHooks run on the real loop. The renderer and TerminalService write to the terminal. JSX never paints the terminal directly.
sections.code:
JSX component
  → compileToComponent / toView
  → Model / Update / View (MVU)  ← RuntimeHooks
  → Renderer + TerminalService

sections.heading: Named runes and the model
sections.body: Call $state with an initial value and a name. Call $states with a record of named values. Both create model fields. Call $set to push a set message into MVU. During the view phase, beginViewHydration aligns paint with the model.

sections.heading: Terminal I/O ownership
sections.body: The core package owns service Tags. It also owns pure capability helpers, graphics helpers, and Live service implementations. The platform package is the public facade. Apps import Live services and capability helpers from @tuix/platform.

sections.heading: Terminal capabilities
sections.body: Call detectCapabilities with env data and optional probe results. The function is pure. You can unit-test it without a TTY. The live terminal applies TUIX_PROBE_* environment overrides. Use parsePrimaryDA for Device Attributes probe responses.

sections.heading: PTY
sections.body: ProcessManager with config.pty spawns interactive terminals. The production path uses the node-pty backend. Use writePty and resizePty on the manager path.

sections.heading: Specs and quality
sections.body: Authoritative design lives under the spec directory. Architecture, runtime, JSX, terminal, quality gates, and catalogs each have a section. Release gates require architecture tests, full bun test, typecheck of delivery entries, and lint across packages, apps, docs, scripts, and tests.

cli.title: CLI
cli.description: Run the tuix command-line interface for help, version, and dashboard.

sections.heading: What the CLI is
sections.body: The tuix binary is the framework dogfood CLI. It ships from the @tuix/bin package. Use it to inspect the install and to open interactive tools.

sections.heading: Commands
sections.body: Print help with --help. Print the version with version. Open the interactive help explorer with help. Open live system metrics with dashboard.
sections.code:
tuix --help
tuix version
tuix help
tuix dashboard

sections.heading: One-shot versus interactive
sections.body: One-shot commands exit after paint. Examples are version and --help. Interactive commands use fullscreen Model-View-Update (MVU). Examples are help and dashboard.

sections.heading: Help explorer controls
sections.body: In the help explorer, move with the arrow keys or j and k. Confirm with Enter. Quit with q. Selection updates through named $state and bindMvuPush.

sections.heading: Run from the monorepo
sections.body: From a monorepo checkout, call the CLI through Bun. Use bun run tuix or the package entry file under packages/bin.
sections.code:
bun run tuix --help
bun packages/bin/src/bin/tuix.ts version

capabilities.title: Terminal & graphics
capabilities.description: Detect terminal capabilities, encode graphics, and handle input, paste, and PTY.

sections.heading: What this guide covers
sections.body: Tuix measures what the terminal can do. It selects a graphics protocol. It streams keys, mouse, paste, resize, and focus. It can spawn a Pseudo-Terminal (PTY) for interactive child processes.

sections.heading: detectCapabilities
sections.body: Call detectCapabilities with environment variables and optional size or probe data. The function returns a TerminalCapabilities value. The function is pure. Live terminal code can apply TUIX_PROBE_* overrides after detection.

sections.heading: Graphics protocols
sections.body: Call selectGraphicsProtocol with the capabilities value. Call encodeGraphics with pixel data and the same capabilities. The helpers pick a protocol the terminal supports.

sections.heading: Device Attributes probes
sections.body: Use parsePrimaryDA helpers on probe responses. Feed the parse result into the same capability shape. This path supports terminals that answer Device Attributes queries.

sections.heading: Input stream
sections.body: Live InputService streams keys, mouse, paste, resize, and focus. readLine uses a continuous PubSub subscription. Multi-character lines complete when the user presses Enter. Bracketed paste and focus CSI I/O parse on the live path.

sections.heading: PTY processes
sections.body: Set config.pty on ProcessManager to spawn an interactive TTY. The production backend is node-pty. Call writePty to send data. Call resizePty when the terminal size changes.

sections.heading: Where to import
sections.body: Import detectCapabilities, encodeGraphics, selectGraphicsProtocol, and LiveServices from @tuix/platform. The core package owns the physical Live implementations and pure helpers.

testing.title: Testing
testing.description: Run unit tests, architecture checks, and the end-to-end PTY harness.

sections.heading: What you test
sections.body: Tuix ships unit tests, architecture boundary tests, catalog honesty tests, and an end-to-end harness. Use bun test as the test runner.

sections.heading: Unit and architecture tests
sections.body: Run the full monorepo suite with bun test. Run architecture tests to enforce package dependency direction. Run catalog honesty tests to check module status against the catalog.
sections.code:
bun test
bun test tests/architecture
bun test tests/catalog-honesty.test.ts

sections.heading: End-to-end harness
sections.body: Import createTestHarness from @tuix/testing. The harness spawns a PTY session for CLI smoke tests. You can send keys, wait for text, and capture screenshots.

sections.heading: What architecture tests enforce
sections.body: Architecture tests check that lower layers do not import higher layers. They also check source import boundaries for packages. Failures mean a package crossed a layer boundary.

sections.heading: Release gates
sections.body: Release gates live in spec/60-quality/RELEASE_GATES.md. Gates require architecture tests, full bun test, typecheck of delivery load and build entries, and lint over packages, apps, docs, scripts, and tests.

sections.heading: How to run checks before a change
sections.body: Install dependencies. Run bun test. Run typecheck. Run lint. Fix failures before you merge.
sections.code:
bun install
bun test
bun run typecheck
bun run lint

packages-overview.title: Packages
packages-overview.description: Choose @tuix packages by layer for foundation, runtime, authoring, and ecosystem.

sections.heading: Layers
sections.body: Tuix packages sit in four layers. Foundation is ansi, core, input, platform, and storage. Runtime is view, runtime, and reactive. Authoring is jsx, ui, and themes. Ecosystem is process-manager, config, logger, coordination, update, telemetry, debug, testing, docs, bin, and app-presets. Lower layers never import higher layers.

sections.heading: Foundation packages
sections.body: Use @tuix/core for types, errors, service contracts, Live I/O, capabilities, and graphics. Use @tuix/platform as the public facade for LiveServices and capability helpers. Use @tuix/ansi for colors, styles, and borders. Use @tuix/input for keyboard and mouse parse utilities. Use @tuix/storage for memory and filesystem backends.

sections.heading: Runtime packages
sections.body: Use @tuix/view for render and layout primitives. Use @tuix/runtime for the Model-View-Update (MVU) loop, commands, subscriptions, and hooks. Use @tuix/reactive for runes, the $set bridge into MVU, and key handlers.

sections.heading: Authoring packages
sections.body: Use @tuix/jsx for the JSX runtime and the compile bridge. Use @tuix/ui for widgets such as Help, LargeText, Viewport, and forms. Use @tuix/themes for theme tokens.

sections.heading: Ecosystem packages
sections.body: Use @tuix/process-manager for process lifecycle and PTY. Use @tuix/config for JSON, YAML, TOML, and env config. Use @tuix/testing for harnesses and end-to-end PTY sessions. Use @tuix/bin for the tuix CLI. Other packages cover logging, coordination, updates, telemetry, debug, docs, and app presets.

sections.heading: How to choose a package
sections.body: Start with @tuix/platform, @tuix/jsx, @tuix/runtime, @tuix/reactive, and @tuix/view for a typical app. Import Live services and capabilities from platform, not from core. Add @tuix/ui and @tuix/themes when you need widgets and tokens. Add @tuix/process-manager when you spawn PTY children. Add @tuix/config when you load app configuration. Add @tuix/testing when you write harness or end-to-end tests.

sections.heading: Minimal install set
sections.body: Add the five packages most apps need. Expand only when a feature requires another package.

sections.heading: Catalog
sections.body: Module status and feature IDs live in spec/20-catalog/MODULE_CATALOG.md. Catalog honesty tests enforce that the catalog matches the packages.
